articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Sunday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions
articles.summary: The intensity and drama of the 2026 Little League World Series (LLWS) has been ratcheted up this weekend. Saturday brought the first elimination games of the tournament, and Sunday will bring the spotlight to contenders from the winners' brackets.
articles.body:
The intensity and drama of the 2026 Little League World Series (LLWS) has been ratcheted up this weekend. Saturday brought the first elimination games of the tournament, and Sunday will bring the spotlight to contenders from the winners' brackets.

The double-elimination is once again broken down into United States and International brackets. The winner of each will face off in the LLWS Championship on Sunday, August 30.

Here, you'll find a preview of Sunday's action—which includes the MLB Little League Classic—along with tournament information, scheduling info, and some predictions.

Asian-Pacific Region: West Seoul (B) LL (Seoul, South Korea)

Australia Region: Ryde Little League (Sydney, New South Wales)

Canada Region: Little Mountain LLC (Vancouver, British Columbia)

Caribbean Region: Los Nacionales LL (Santiago, Dominican Republic)

Curaçao Region: Pariba LL (Willemstad, Curaçao)

Europe and Africa Region: South Czech Republic LL (Brno, Czechia)

Latin American Region: Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Águila LL (León, Nicaragua)

Mexico Region: Municipal De Tijuana LL (Tijuana, Baja California)

Panama Region: David Doleguita LL (Chiriquí, Panama)

Great Lakes Region: West Side LL (Hamilton, Ohio)

Metro Region: Bayonne Central LL (Bayonne, New Jersey)

Mid-Atlantic Region: East Side LL (West Chester, Pennsylvania)

Midwest Region: Davenport Northwest LL (Davenport, Iowa)

Mountain Region: Paseo Verde LL (Henderson, Nevada)

New England Region: Bridgewater Joe Lozaro LL (Bridgewater, Massachusetts)

Northwest Region: Soundview LL (Tacoma, Washington)

Southeast Region: Phenix City Youth Baseball LL (Phenix City, Alabama)

Southwest Region: Boerne LL (Boerne, Texas)

West Region: Sweetwater Valley LL (Bonita, California)

Great Lakes Region 10, New England Region 0

Little League Classic: Atlanta Braves vs. Milwaukee Brewers

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Sunday's opener will pit Paseo Verde Little League of Henderson, Nevada (Mountain Region) against Soundview Little League of Tacoma, Washington.

Soundview has taken the tough road to this point, notching 2-0 and 4-3 victories over the Southeast and Southwest regions, respectively. Paseo Verde, meanwhile, delivered a 6-5 walk-off win over the Great Lakes on Friday to advance. Both teams have shown the ability to win tight contests, so this should be a fun matchup to start the day.

The second morning match will feature Municipal De Tijuana Little League of Tijuana in a matchup with Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Águila Little League of León, Nicaragua.

On paper, this is a less-even matchup. The Latin America representative eked through close contests against the Caribbean and Panama, while Mexico is coming off a 7-1 romp over Australia.

Game 3 will feature Davenport Northwest Little League of Davenport, Iowa, a team that is coming off a combined no-hitter against the West region. Davenport will take on a Bayonne Central Little League team that has notched 2-1 and 3-1 victories over the New England and Mid-Atlantic regions.

Bayonne's first victory of the tournament came in walk-off fashion.

Sunday's last tournament game will pit West Seoul Little League of South Korea against Pariba Little League of Willemstad, Curaçao.

Willemstad has produced two of the last four LLWC runners-up, and Pariba is coming off a dominant 6-0 shutout of Japan. However, West Seoul has looked like one of the best squads in the tournament while winning 7-0 and 5-0 against Canada and Europe-Africa, respectively.

Sunday's nightcap will be Major League Baseball's annual Little League Classic, featuring the Atlanta Braves and Milwaukee Brewers at historic Bowman Field.

articles.title: 10 Biggest Disappointments of MLB Season After 5 Months
articles.summary: Heading into the 2026 Major League Baseball season, Garrett Crochet was a top candidate for AL Cy Young, Framber Valdez was going to save the Tigers, Marcell Ozuna felt like the possible final piece of a Pittsburgh Pirates postseason puzzle and a Mets-Mariners World Series looked like a very real possibility.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2026 Major League Baseball season, Garrett Crochet was a top candidate for AL Cy Young, Framber Valdez was going to save the Tigers, Marcell Ozuna felt like the possible final piece of a Pittsburgh Pirates postseason puzzle and a Mets-Mariners World Series looked like a very real possibility.

Predictions and expectations go haywire all the time, but some disappointments are much larger than others. Ahead, we've ranked the top 10 as we slowly but surely approach the finish line of this MLB campaign.

Before we dive into the rankings, though, we need to touch on some 'honorable' mentions in order for this list to feel complete.

Athletics —The A's had a .500 record in mid-June, but they have since become a laughingstock. Every other team in the majors has won at least 21 games since June 20, but the A's are 11-42 and now have the worst record of all at 49-80.

Edward Cabrera, RHP, Chicago Cubs —Cabrera is on the IL for the third time this season, twice for blisters and once for a hamstring/adductor. And in the nine starts he has been able to make since the beginning of May, he has a 7.97 ERA. Staying healthy always has been a struggle for him, but he's usually much better than this when available.

Edwin Díaz, RHP, Los Angeles Dodgers —Frankly, you could argue that Díaz and his 11.85 ERA belong at No. 1 on this list. However, we're cutting him a bit of slack, because he clearly wasn't healthy either before or after the surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow. Either way, though, the Dodgers definitely have not gotten what they paid for here.

Gunnar Henderson, SS, Baltimore Orioles —Henderson certainly hasn't been bad , but he is a shell of his former self, struggling to even keep his OPS at .700. Steamer had him projected as the third-most valuable position player in the majors in the preseason. Instead, he is only one of Baltimore's three most valuable position players because they traded away Adley Rutschman and Taylor Ward.

Tatsuya Imai, RHP, Houston Astros —In his final season in Japan, Imai had a 1.92 ERA, 0.89 WHIP and averaged just a shade under four strikeouts per walk. But he has been handing out walks left and right in the majors, recently losing his spot in the Astros rotation after failing to survive the first inning for a third time.

Kansas City Royals —The injury bug has been none too kind to the Royals, most notably in the form of another mostly lost season for former ace Cole Ragans. They also lost closer Carlos Estévez practically on Opening Day. Every team battles injury, though, and not all of them crash and burn like the Royals have.

Paul Skenes, RHP, Pittsburgh Pirates —Hard to justify putting him in the top 10 when he was still an All-Star and has still been one of Pittsburgh's five most valuable players this season. But Skenes' regression from "Elite" to "Meh" over the past three months has become an inescapable narrative.

Trea Turner, SS, Philadelphia Phillies —He has 17 home runs and 17 stolen bases, but he's nowhere near the consistent hitter that he used to be. And after putting forth a great season with his glove in 2025, he has been one of the worst defensive shortstops in 2026. (Only seven years left on that contract...)

10. Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 1B, Toronto Blue Jays

From 2021-25, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. racked up 159 home runs in 3,463 trips to the plate. That's one for every 21.8 plate appearances—a far cry from Aaron Judge at a PA/HR ratio of 12.7, but a good deal better than the MLB-wide average of 32.5.

This year, though, Guerrero has needed nearly 70 plate appearances per home run. And though he did have a few at Rogers Centre during the 2025 postseason, it has now been more than a full calendar year since he last hit a home run at home during the regular season.

And, to be clear, it isn't just the sharp decline in home runs that have made him one of the biggest disappointments. He also has his worst batting average and on-base percentage since 2020, presently saddled with a .693 OPS after posting an .879 mark over the past half-decade.

He's still roughly league average in terms of barrel rate, exit velocity, hard-hit percentage and expected slugging. But let's just say the Blue Jays didn't give Guerrero $500M because of his ability to be league average in those departments.

9. Marcell Ozuna, DH, Pittsburgh Pirates

Over his final three seasons with Atlanta, Marcell Ozuna accumulated 100 home runs and 272 RBI with an .867 OPS. He ranked ninth in the majors in dingers, 22nd in ribbies and was 13th in OPS, one point ahead of Kyle Schwarber.

Even though his 2025 campaign was nowhere near as impressive as his 2023 and 2024, Pittsburgh hoped it was getting a steal at DH when it gave Ozuna a one-year, $12M contract in mid-February.

What it got, however, was a designated hitter who was designated for assignment earlier this month with a career-worst .612 OPS and just eight home runs in 280 trips to the plate.

They were originally playing him almost every day, but started predominantly deploying him against left-handed starters in June and July. Even that did next to nothing to spark some life in his bat, and they finally gave up the ghost right after the trade deadline.

What's wild, though, is that in spite of Ozuna's complete lack of production, the Pirates are on pace to score 228 more runs than last season. It's a remarkable turnaround, but it could have been so much better if they had spent just a little bit more for Kazuma Okamoto or Munetaka Murakami instead.

Late last season, the Braves scooped Ha-Seong Kim off waivers from the Rays. He wasn't anything special for them, but he was just good enough in September that they elected to re-sign him on a one-year, $20M deal, hoping he would be their everyday shortstop.

Unfortunately, he suffered a torn tendon in his finger in a freak accident about a month later and ended up missing the first seven weeks of the regular season.

And since returning, he has put together one of the worst seasons in MLB history with a triple slash of .066/.165/.066.

If he stays there, Kim would be the first player to slug below .080 in a season of at least 80 plate appearances since Kevin Brown in 2000. And, well, Kevin Brown was a pitcher. Kim would be the first non-pitcher ever to slug under .080 while making at least 80 plate appearances.

At least he hasn't committed any more errors after recording three in his first seven games back, but it's hard to believe they have not yet admitted defeat by designating him for assignment.

7. Zac Gallen and Merrill Kelly, RHPs, Arizona Diamondbacks

The Diamondbacks are seven games above .500 and hanging around in the NL wild card race.

But, man, imagine where they might be in the standings if they were getting anything good out of the two pitchers they re-signed this past winter to salaries of at least $20M.

At least Merrill Kelly is presently healthy, second on the team in innings pitched. But in his 23 starts, the Snakes have gone 9-14, thanks to career-worst marks in ERA (5.37), WHIP (1.52) and K/9 (5.9). Of his seven quality starts, only three have come since Memorial Day.

Gallen might be done for the year, on the IL with elbow inflammation since just before the All-Star Break. It certainly was not a first half to remember, either, also saddled with career-worst marks across the board: 6.34 ERA, 1.56 WHIP, 5.6 K/9. Arizona has gone 6-13 in his 19 starts, only three of which were of the quality variety.

Whether you prefer FanGraphs or Baseball-Reference as your source of WAR, both Kelly and Gallen have been worth wins below replacement.

Over the past four seasons, the Giants have been the definition of mediocre: two years at 81-81, one at 80-82 and one at 79-83. The expectation heading into 2026 was more of the same, with a preseason win total of 80.5.

Even though they weren't supposed to be a World Series threat, the Giants have managed to become one of the biggest disappointments by flirting with not only the worst record in baseball this season, but plausibly the most losses in a single season in this franchise's 144-year history.

Their current record in futility was 100 losses in 1985, and they are presently on a full-season pace for 96. However, they've lost 14 of their last 19 and have one of the toughest remaining schedules in the business. Going 9-25 (or worse) the rest of the way isn't exactly tough to envision.

The underperforming hasn't been contained to any specific player—though Rafael Devers sure drew a lot of the ire back when he finished April with a .537 OPS. The high-paid stars simply haven't been quite as valuable as expected. And with the exception of Luis Arraez blossoming into one of the most coveted players ahead of the trade deadline, there haven't been any surprise breakouts on this roster, either.

Just a widespread letdown in year No. 1 of the Tony Vitello experiment. We shall see if there ends up being a year No. 2.

When the Tigers landed Framber Valdez on a three-year, $115M deal in early February, it felt like one of the biggest turning points of the entire offseason.

After months of Tarik Skubal trade speculations, Detroit loudly announced that it was all-in on winning in 2026. Behind the strength of what FanGraphs projected as the second-best starting rotation in the majors, the Tigers immediately became the clear favorite to win the AL Central, as well as a trendy pick to crash the World Series.

However, Valdez simply never became the co-ace that they needed him to be—particularly during that six-week stretch in which Skubal was recovering from his elbow scope.

That's when it all went downhill in a hurry for the Tigers, who went 6-22 in May. They lost all five of Valdez's starts that month while he gave them a 5.93 ERA, including that infamous meltdown against the Red Sox that pretty much jump-started Detroit's fall from grace.

And then in late July—when Detroit was straddling the fence between buying and selling—Valdez opened the second half with a complete disaster against the Cubs (0.2 IP, 6 ER) and a subsequent less than ace-like outing against the last-place Royals (5.0 IP, 3 R). The Tigers lost both games and ultimately decided a few days later to sell off Skubal and Casey Mize in preparation for the future.

On the whole, Valdez's numbers haven't been terrible . But he has the highest AAV among American League pitchers, and his performance hasn't even remotely justified that status.

Kyle Tucker signing a four-year, $240M contract with the Dodgers was a breaking point for a lot of MLB fans.

The deal was announced on Jan. 21, which just so happened to also be the deadline for the Dodgers to make their $169M tax payment to MLB for laughably outspending everyone else in 2025. And in their quest for a three-peat, giving Tucker the highest present-day AAV contract in MLB history all but ensured they will be making an even bigger tax payment for their 2026 spending.

Tucker's luxury tax figure on their payroll is $57.195M, per Spotrac . And because they were already well above the highest tax bracket possible, the Dodgers have to pay a $1.10 tax for every dollar of that luxury tax figure, or a $62.9145M penalty. His actual cash salary for the year is $55M, so he is individually costing them a staggering $117.9145M in 2026—which is higher than the estimated tax payrolls of the Marlins, Guardians, Cardinals, Rays or White Sox.

But if you're among the throngs who have been up in arms about the Dodgers' payroll/deferral practices, you've at least been able to enjoy a chuckle at the fact that for nearly $120M, Tucker has been worth precisely 0.0 wins above replacement for them.

From 2021-25, Tucker had an OPS of .878, good for 10th-best among players with at least 2,000 plate appearances. He averaged 32.8 home runs and 25.7 stolen bases per 162 games played. This year, though, he has a .690 OPS, operating at a 162-game pace of 14.7 home runs and 9.4 stolen bases.

Of course, it hasn't done anything to slow them down. While the Dodgers haven't been as dominant as anticipated, they entered play on Saturday just two games behind the Brewers for the best record in baseball, well on their way to a first-round bye in spite of Tucker's mediocrity.

3. Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony, Boston Red Sox

Shortly before Opening Day, MLB.com asked its 57 experts to predict who would win the various major awards for 2026.

Boston's Garrett Crochet was their pick for AL Cy Young, edging out twice-reigning Tarik Skubal by a margin of one vote. Crochet led the majors with 255 strikeouts in 2025, this after he averaged 12.9 K/9 in 2024, which had been the eighth-highest mark in MLB history for a season with at least 140 innings pitched.

And though Bobby Witt Jr. was the pick for AL MVP, Boston's Roman Anthony placed fifth in that vote, fresh on the heels of his impressive showing in the World Baseball Classic.

No other Red Sox player received a vote for MVP, Cy Young or ROY. Needless to say, that duo was supposed to anchor Boston's quest for the AL No. 1 seed.

But Crochet has been on the IL since late April; Anthony since early May. The former was shelled in three of his six starts and has a 6.30 ERA. The latter looked nothing like he did last season, hitting just one home run and posting a .675 OPS in his 30 games played.

Instead of carrying the team, their combined shortcomings were perhaps the biggest reason Boston had a 13-21 record the last time we saw either of them in action.

Both are hoping to return in September, with Crochet likely to inhabit a spot in the bullpen if he does make it back. But will they help or hurt the Red Sox in October?

2. Cal Raleigh, C (and the Seattle Mariners in General)

Cal Raleigh clubbed a crucial three-run home run in Seattle's victory over the Cubs on Friday night. The Mariners have now won each of the last seven times Raleigh has homered, five of them by a single run.

Conversely, the Big Dumper entered that game triple-slashing .104/.283/.229 in the month of August and with a .569 OPS for the season, so you'll have to forgive us for not being willing to believe that this is finally where Raleigh and Mariners start to turn things around.

The first runner-up for AL MVP in 2025 hasn't had a three-game hitting streak since July 4-8, nor have the M's put together a three-game winning streak more recently than July 18-20.

In fact, since winning eight in a row from May into June, Seattle has gone 28-39 overall, averaging 3.58 runs per game. While Raleigh's historic regression is most to blame for that, neither Julio Rodríguez nor Josh Naylor has done much to help matters. Luke Raley and Colt Emerson had also been dreadful, each with an OPS in the .400s from June 3 onward prior to both landing on the IL.

Worse yet, since the aforementioned winning streak in mid-July, even Seattle's once-elite pitching staff has been a hot mess, allowing nearly six runs per game.

Granted, the recent 22-0 shellacking at the hands of Milwaukee drove up that average by about 0.5 runs. But even if that game hadn't happened, the Mariners would have still allowed more runs over the past five weeks than every team except the A's and Rockies.

It's almost hard to believe this is the same team that entered the year as basically co-favorites with the Yankees to represent the AL in the World Series.

For as poorly as things have gone for the Seattle Mariners, at least they still have a tangible playoff pulse, entering play on Saturday four games back in the AL West and three games back for the AL's final wild card spot. With the benefit of 17 games remaining against the A's, Angels and Rockies, PECOTA even had the M's at a 50.5 percent chance of making the postseason.

But the New York Mets—who entered the season with a 90.5 win total and a $375M tax payroll , both good for highest among all teams not named the Dodgers—are as good as dead for postseason purposes (and have been for a while) at 11 games back.

Their six most noteworthy offseason moves were (in no particular order) trading for Freddy Peralta, signing Bo Bichette, trading for Luis Robert Jr., signing Devin Williams, trading for Marcus Semien and signing Jorge Polanco.

Baseball-Reference puts that sextet's cumulative value "added" at a minus-1.1 wins above replacement.

On top of that, Francisco Lindor missed two months with a calf injury and hasn't made his usual impact when healthy, Mark Vientos regressed even further from last year's fall from grace, Brett Baty vanished after last year's breakout and both David Peterson and Kodai Senga pitched their way out of the starting rotation in a hurry.

Throw in Juan Soto's multiple trips to the IL and this season has gone about as sideways as it possibly could have for the Mets.

The only redeeming silver lining is that rookies Nolan McLean, A.J. Ewing, Carson Benge and Zac Thornton have all made a positive impact. So, too, has Christian Scott in his return from Tommy John surgery.

However, five twenty-somethings breaking out while making less than $800,000 apiece should have been the cherry on a World Series sundae for the Mets, not the only thing about this season that wasn't a disaster.

articles.title: White Sox's Jake Rogers, Emma Rodriguez Meet After Video 'Losing' Belongings While Catching HR Ball
articles.summary: The woman who went viral for losing items from her purse while celebrating a walk-off home run by Chicago White Sox catcher Jake Rogers on Friday met up with the veteran backstop and executed a trade on Sunday.
articles.body:
The woman who went viral for losing items from her purse while celebrating a walk-off home run by Chicago White Sox catcher Jake Rogers on Friday met up with the veteran backstop and executed a trade on Sunday.

As seen in a post by the White Sox on X, Emma Rodriguez traded the home run ball to Rogers for what looks to be an autographed jersey and bat, plus another ball:

Rodriguez made a splash on social media Friday because the White Sox broadcast showed her jumping up and down with the home run ball in her hand, while items flew out of her purse:

She later took to X to show off the ball and to confirm that she was able to recover everything that fell out of her purse:

White Sox on-field reporter Brooke Fletcher followed up with a report that Rodriguez messaged Rogers on Instagram in hopes of getting the ball autographed, which led to their meeting and trade on Sunday since Rogers actually wanted the ball himself:

The home run was only the 48th of Rogers' MLB career and his first as a member of the White Sox.

After playing for the Detroit Tigers since 2019, the 31-year-old Rogers was traded to the Baltimore Orioles in July. He was then traded to the Boston Red Sox shortly thereafter and claimed off waivers by the White Sox this month.

Rogers hit the home run in only his sixth game as a member of the team, and it was a huge one give where the White Sox are in the standings.

Entering play on Sunday, Chicago leads the American League Central with a 67-62 record, placing it 3.5 games ahead of the second-place Cleveland Guardians.

articles.title: New Shohei Ohtani Pitching Update, Dodgers' Dave Roberts Reveals Timeline for Star to Pitch in Game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes it could only be a matter of days before Shohei Ohtani is back to pitching in MLB games.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes it could only be a matter of days before Shohei Ohtani is back to pitching in MLB games.

Roberts told reporters Sunday that Ohtani's return to the mound could arrive as early as next week.

According to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya and Katie Woo , Los Angeles is considering starting Ohtani and having him throw one inning against the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 30.

The four-time MVP had a throwing session against hitters on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.

Ohtani hasn't pitched since the Dodgers' 4-3 win over the San Diego Padres on July 3. He was initially sidelined because of knee trouble, and team doctors also flagged a biceps injury in his throwing arm.

Ohtani has continued to serve as the designated hitter in the interim, and his performance hasn't suffered much despite not being at 100 percent. Across 20 games so far in August, he has six home runs and a .282/.371/.564 slash line.

Welcoming the six-time All-Star back as a two-way player would be a huge boost to the starting rotation.

The Dodgers' acquisition of Tarik Skubal was a case of the rich getting richer, but the pitching staff was also an area of concern. At the time of the trade, the trio of Ohtani, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow were unavailable, while Justin Wrobleski had soared past his career high for innings in a single MLB season.

L.A. has since welcomed Snell back from the injured list, but Wrobleski landed on the IL with left forearm inflammation.

For as much as some fans think a three-peat is almost preordained, the Dodgers pitching staff isn't in a great place right now. The situation is much different if Ohtani gets the green light and remains the player who posted a 1.79 ERA and averaged 10 strikeouts per nine innings before going down.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Sunday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: The 2026 Little League World Series continued on Sunday from Williamsport, PA, with a four-game slate.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series continued on Sunday from Williamsport, PA, with a four-game slate.

Thanks to the double-elimination format, Sunday wasn't the end-all, be-all for any team, but others managed to gain momentum on the march to next week's championship final.

Here's a look at Sunday's full schedule and results. The full bracket can be found on the Little League World Series official website .

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Mountain (Henderson, NV) def. Northwest (Tacoma, WA), 5-0

Latin America (Nicaragua) def. Mexico, 8-4

Midwest (Davenport, IA) def. Metro (Bayonne, N.J.), 6-0

Curaçao def. Asia-Pacific (South Korea), 1-0

After a one-run win in their last game, Nevada left no doubt this time around.

A five-run fifth inning and five strikeouts from Brooks McFarland spearheaded Nevada's shutout victory over Washington.

The Mountain Region representatives will look to keep the momentum going in the next round, while Washington will have to fight its way out of the loser's bracket.

Nicaragua stifled a high-powered Mexico team that produced seven runs in its previous game to advance.

The game was tight until Nicaragua broke it open with a bases-loaded two-run double in the fifth inning:

Nicaragua has scored a combined 14 runs over its last two games, and it will look to stay hot in the next round.

Iowa halted New Jersey's Cinderella journey behind a massive effort from Anthony Johnson Jr., both on the mound and at the plate.

In addition to launching a three-run home run, Johnson pitched a shutout with a whopping 15 strikeouts to spearhead the victory.

New Jersey will now try to fight its way out of the loser's bracket when it faces the winner of Monday's game between Ohio and Texas.

Curaçao and South Korea battled in a tense game, but one run was all Curaçao needed to advance.

After scratching across a run in the first inning, Juriënsly De Windt and Giendry Ryan combined for 10 strikeouts in a shutout victory.

Curaçao's next challenge will be to stifle the scorching-hot Nicaragua squad when the teams return to action in the winner's bracket on Wednesday.

articles.title: Mariners' Brendan Donovan Placed on Concussion IL After Being Hit in Head in Batting Cage
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners will be without utilityman Brendan Donovan in the immediate future after he was hit in the head by a pitch in the batting cages ahead of Saturday's game against the Chicago Cubs.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners will be without utilityman Brendan Donovan in the immediate future after he was hit in the head by a pitch in the batting cages ahead of Saturday's game against the Chicago Cubs.

Andrew Destin of the Associated Press reported Seattle placed Donovan on the seven-day concussion injured list Sunday.

"It was just one of those situations that's unfortunate," Mariners manager Dan Wilson said. "But he will be back hopefully as soon as possible."

Seattle scratched Donovan from its lineup Saturday and recalled Patrick Wisdom from Triple-A Tacoma to replace him on the roster.

It is another setback for the utilityman, who came to the Mariners via a three-team trade with the St. Louis Cardinals and Tampa Bay Rays during the offseason. Yet he dealt with groin issues early in the season and has played just 39 games.

He is slashing .277/.371/.409 with three home runs and 15 RBI in those contests.

Despite the late scratch for Donovan, the Mariners still beat the Cubs on Saturday and have a chance to finish the three-game sweep Sunday.

They are still six games under .500 at 62-68 but just three games back of the first-place Houston Astros in the American League West.

articles.title: Breaking Down MLB Playoff Picture 2026, Standings and Current Postseason Bracket
articles.summary: The MLB playoff picture continues to take shape as the regular season barrels toward an exciting finish.
articles.body:
The MLB playoff picture continues to take shape as the regular season barrels toward an exciting finish.

While the Milwaukee Brewers lead the National League, they closed out this week's slate of action with a Sunday Night Baseball loss to the Atlanta Braves, who lead the NL East.

Here's a look at the latest standings and what to watch for down the stretch of the 2026 season.

The AL West has become the division to watch after a surprising 2-6 stretch by the Houston Astros, who are now tied with the Texas Rangers for first place.

The Astros dropped two out of three games against the lowly Athletics, losing Sunday's series finale 7-6 after the Athletics overcame a 6-0 deficit.

While the Rangers are now fighting for the division crown, they're also clinging to the last AL Wild Card spot thanks to their tiebreaker over the Cleveland Guardians, who have won four straight games.

Over in the National League, the Philadelphia Phillies are making things interesting as they close the gap with the Braves for the NL East lead. After winning their ninth straight game on Sunday with a six-run ninth inning for a comeback victory over the St. Louis Cardinals, the Phillies are the hottest team in baseball.

It will be exciting to watch things play out down the stretch as the playoffs draw nearer, and teams will try to maneuver up the standings over the next few weeks.

articles.title: Little League Classic Matchup Announced for 2027 MLB Season, Teams and Date Revealed
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs will face the Toronto Blue Jays at next season's Little League Classic in Williamsport, MLB announced Sunday.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs will face the Toronto Blue Jays at next season's Little League Classic in Williamsport, MLB announced Sunday.

This year's Little League Classic was held between the Atlanta Braves and Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday.

The Little League Classic has been played every season since 2017, with the exception of 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Cubs appeared in the contest once back in 2017, a 7-1 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates. The Blue Jays have never appeared in the showcase.

Both the Pittsburgh Pirates and Philadelphia Phillies have appeared in the contest twice, which makes sense as MLB's two Pennsylvania representatives. The New York Mets have also played in the game twice.

Obviously one of the looming questions regarding any future dates is the possibility of a lost season due to ongoing labor disagreements between MLB's owners and the player's union. With the owners pushing for a salary cap, a lockout is perhaps on the horizon , putting the status of games like the 2027 Little League Classic very much up in the air.

articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series continues Monday in Williamsport, Pennsylvania with several teams looking to stave off elimination and keep their title aspirations alive.

Who are they and when can viewers check out all of the action?

Find out with this preview of the day's lineup.

Great Lakes Region: West Side LL (Hamilton, Ohio)

Metro Region: Bayonne Central LL (Bayonne, New Jersey)

Mid-Atlantic Region: East Side LL (West Chester, Pennsylvania)

Midwest Region: Davenport Northwest LL (Davenport, Iowa)

Mountain Region: Paseo Verde, LL (Henderson, Nevada)

New England Region: Bridgewater Joe Lozaro LL (Bridgewater, Massachusetts)

Northwest Region: Soundview LL (Tacoma, Washington)

Southeast Region: Phenix City Youth Baseball LL (Phenix City, Alabama)

Southwest Region: Boerne LL (Boerne, Texas)

West Region: Sweetwater Valley LL (Bonita, California)

Asian-Pacific Region: West Seoul (B) LL (Seoul, South Korea)

Australia Region: Ryde Little League (Sydney, New South Wales)

Canada Region: Little Mountain LLC (Vancouver, British Columbia)

Caribbean Region: Los Nacionales LL (Santiago, Dominican Republic)

Curaçao Region: Pariba LL (Willemstad, Curaçao)

Europe and Africa Region: South Czech Republic LL (Brno, Czechia)

Latin American Region: Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Aguila LL (Leon, Nicaragua)

Mexico Region: Municipal De Tijuana LL (Tijuana, Baja California)

Panama Region: David Doleguita LL (Chiriquí, Panama)

Game 21: Panama vs. Canada (1:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Canada)

Game 22: Great Lakes vs. Southwest (3:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Southwest)

Game 23: Japan vs. Europe-Africa (5:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Japan)

Game 24: Southeast vs. Mid-Atlantic (7:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Mid-Atlantic)

Two international powerhouses battled Sunday at Volunteer Stadium as Curaçao squared off with South Korea, each looking to continue their unbeaten streaks in this year's tournament.

It was Curaçao that would emerge victoriously on the strength of the performances from pitchers Juriënsly De Windt and Giendry Ryan, who combined for a complete-game shutout of the powerful South Korean squad.

The duo delivered 10 strikeouts, while Ryan added a double at the plate.

It was an outstanding victory for Curaçao, which looks every bit a contender to leave Williamsport with the country's second LLWS title.

That game capped off a day of action that saw Bayonne, New Jersey, shut out in its first tournament loss to Davenport, Iowa.

articles.title: New 2026 MLB Playoff Seeding and World Series Predictions With 5 Weeks to Go
articles.summary: With barely a month remaining until the 2026 MLB postseason begins, the bracket is beginning to feel a bit more solidified.
articles.body:
With barely a month remaining until the 2026 MLB postseason begins, the bracket is beginning to feel a bit more solidified.

Not all 12 spots in the field, mind you. Arizona vs. San Diego for the NL's No. 6 seed looks destined to come right down to the wire, the AL West remains a three-way free-for-all, and you may as well just throw a dart at your best guess for the third and final AL wild-card spot.

However, nine teams have at least a 90 percent chance of making the playoffs, and the rest is slowly but surely taking shape.

What will the final playoff seeding look like?

And which teams are best equipped to win the whole shebang?

We'll go division-by-division (plus a wild card breakdown) through the current state of each league before offering up our latest October predictions.

Consensus Division Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday a.m.)

Boston @ Tampa Bay (3 games, Sept. 18-20)

Tampa Bay @ New York (4 games, Sept. 22-24)

Projected Winner: Tampa Bay Rays (earning No. 1 seed)

The Yankees have certainly kept things interesting, gaining 3.5 games on the Rays in a hurry this past week by virtue of a five-game winning streak. But Tampa Bay has managed to counter-punch every Yankees punch for two months at this point, alone in first place on a daily basis going back to June 28.

That series at Yankee Stadium next month looms all sorts of large, though.

The Bronx Bombers are certainly hoping to have Aaron Judge and Max Fried back and at full strength by the time they square off for four games in three days. And should the Yankees sweep that series, they would effectively be gaining 4.5 games on the Rays, as that would also give them a 7-6 edge in the season series for potential tie-breaking purposes.

However, the Rays have done such a phenomenal job of avoiding prolonged cold spells that dropping four straight in New York feels unlikely. And, who knows, they may have already clinched the division by the time that series begins.

Chicago @ Minnesota (3 games, Aug. 28-30)

Detroit @ Minnesota (3 games, Aug. 31-Sept. 2)

Minnesota @ Chicago (3 games, Sept. 4-6)

Detroit @ Cleveland (4 games, Sept. 4-6)

Minnesota @ Detroit (3 games, Sept. 7-9)

Cleveland @ Minnesota (3 games, Sept. 11-13)

Chicago @ Cleveland (3 games, Sept. 14-16)

Detroit @ Chicago (4 games, Sept. 17-20)

Projected Winner: Chicago White Sox (earning No. 2 seed)

As the lone division with four teams plausibly still in the running, the AL Central has, by far, the longest list of remaining head-to-head series that could make a major difference.

In fact, after facing the A's for the next few days, the Twins are about to embark upon a stretch of 15 consecutive games against the White Sox (six), Tigers (six) and Guardians (three). They could go from 5.5 games back to practically running away with this division if they were to catch fire.

At this point, though, it's tough to bet against the White Sox and what has been the highest scoring offense in the American League.

Never would have guessed five months ago that any part of that statement would be true, and we definitely do still have questions about this team's staying power in October with this pitching staff. But they just keep hanging around a few games above .500, which no one else in this division seems capable of doing.

Texas Rangers: 65-66 (Houston holds H2H tiebreaker)

Houston @ Seattle (2 games, Sept. 22-23)

Projected Winner: Seattle Mariners (earning No. 3 seed)

Even before the back-to-back walk-off wins over the Cubs this past weekend, there was one big reason to believe the Mariners might be able to win this thing in spite of their season-long mediocrity: remaining strength of schedule.

The five key games listed above are all home games for the M's. Of the other 26 games left on their slate, 17 come against either the A's (seven), the Angels (seven) or the Rockies (three)—otherwise known as the three worst teams in the majors.

The other three series are against the Phillies, Red Sox and Blue Jays, so we'll see how they fare in those games against teams battling for wild-card spots. Even so, it is the easiest remaining schedule in all of baseball, while both the Rangers and Astros have relatively difficult paths to the finish line.

Can they finally wake up and at least start to resemble the team they were supposed to be? Or are they going to go something like 7-10 against that 17-game gift from the schedule-makers to bring this disappointing season to a depressing end?

Against our better judgment, we're projecting the former.

Current Standings (excluding our projected division winners)

Consensus Postseason Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday a.m.)

Projected Wild Card Teams: New York Yankees as No. 4 seed, Boston Red Sox as No. 5 seed and Toronto Blue Jays as No. 6 seed

The Yankees and the Red Sox pretty well have playoff spots locked up.

Most likely, at least one of the teams from this cluster of mediocrity is going to go on a bit of a run through these final five weeks to end up a few games above .500. And if remaining schedule strength is influencing our forecast in the AL West, it should probably be the difference maker here, too.

To that end, while the Mariners technically have the easiest remaining schedule in terms of combined winning percentage of all remaining opponents, one could very easily argue that it's actually the Blue Jays who have the easiest remaining schedule, as all 30 of their remaining games come against teams who are currently below .500.

After 13 consecutive games against the Rays, Red Sox and Yankees over the past two weeks, they no longer have any games left against those division rivals. They also don't face the White Sox, they don't face the Astros and their only interleague matchup left on the docket is a home series against the Reds.

Can't ask for much better than that. We'll see if they take advantage.

Atlanta @ Philadelphia (4 games, Sept. 4-7)

Philadelphia @ Atlanta (3 games, Sept. 11-13)

Projected Winner: Atlanta Braves (earning No. 3 seed)

Not since April 13 has Atlanta led this division by a margin of less than two games.

Yet, what was a 9.5 game lead less than two weeks ago has turned into a possible photo finish, as the Phillies have gone 16-5 thus far in August with seven massive head-to-head games on the horizon.

Can the Braves weather the storm and perhaps even re-assert their legitimacy as a World Series contender by winning both of those series against the Phillies—as they also won the previous two head-to-head series this season?

It will be interesting to see how the starting rotations line up for those showdowns. If both weather and injuries cooperate between now and then, it's looking like Philadelphia will have Cristopher Sánchez and Zack Wheeler on the mound for the first two games at home, while Atlanta is projected to counter with Chris Sale and Martín Pérez.

In the immortal words of Bart Scott: Can't wait!

Consensus Division Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday AM)

Milwaukee @ Chicago (4 games, Aug. 31-Sept. 3)

Chicago @ Milwaukee (3 games, Sept. 7-9)

Projected Winner: Milwaukee Brewers (earning No. 2 seed)

For a minute there recently, this race got interesting for the first time in a long time.

After leading the NL Central by at least 3.5 games (though never more than 7.5 games) on a daily basis from May 26 through August 11, the Brewers slipped just a little bit, getting swept by the Padres while the Cubs won three straight to get the margin back down to 3.0 games.

But the Brew Crew bounced back, taking three of four from the Dodgers before winning series against both the Mariners and Braves to push back ahead by what might be an insurmountable margin.

They do have seven head-to-head battles remaining. However, unless Chicago goes at least 5-2 in those games, we're probably done here.

San Diego @ Los Angeles (3 games, Sept. 22-24)

Projected Winner: Los Angeles Dodgers (earning No. 1 seed)

It'd be fun to pretend there's a race worth mentioning here, but there isn't. Not only do the Dodgers have the biggest lead of any current division leader, but they have the easiest remaining schedule among the teams in the NL West.

They also have a much easier schedule than the Brewers, which is why we have them projected to finish ahead of Milwaukee in the race for home-field advantage throughout the postseason.

With Tyler Glasnow set to return this week while Shohei Ohtani is nearing a return to the mound of his own, it almost feels inevitable that the Dodgers—who already have won five games in a row—are about to go on the type of tear that reminds everyone why this team was the overwhelming World Series favorite before the regular season began.

Projected Wild Card Teams: Chicago Cubs as No. 4 seed, Philadelphia Phillies as No. 5 seed and San Diego Padres as No. 6 seed

While the race for the final spot in the American League bracket is an eight-car pile-up of teams who don't feel like a legitimate threat to actually do any damage if they make it to October, the National League is shaping up to be a two-horse race out of the NL West.

And here's the fun news: The only remaining series between the Padres and Diamondbacks takes place in San Diego over the final weekend of the regular season, with the season series currently split 5-5.

The Padres already have a two-game lead, though, and they've been the best team in baseball over the past month, sitting at 21-7 dating back to July 24. The once hapless offense has come to life in a big way in recent weeks, and there's still hope that both Joe Musgrove and Nick Pivetta will make it back onto the mound before it's too late.

Whether either of those pitchers can get stretched out enough to start remains to be seen. But even if they're coming back as middle/long relievers, maybe they help bridge the gap to more Mason Miller saves en route to a spot in the postseason.

No. 3 Seattle Mariners over No. 6 Toronto Blue Jays No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 4 New York Yankees

No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays No. 3 Seattle Mariners over No. 2 Chicago White Sox

ALCS : No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 3 Seattle Mariners

If this is actually the way the seeding plays out, how fun would that Wild Card Round be?

A rematch of last year's ALCS and arguably the fiercest rivalry in the sport that also happens to be a rematch from last year's wild card round?

In particular, Boston vs. New York is the one with potential World Series implications, as those certainly feel like the two best teams in the American League, if healthy.

All due respect to Tampa Bay, but Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and Shane McClanahan don't pack the same punch as Cam Schittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried/Carlos Rodón. And no one in the sport has been hotter over the past two months than the Red Sox, at 39-13 in their last 52 games.

Maybe they peaked too early and they're going to flame out before the games truly matter, but betting against Boston coming out of this half of the bracket would feel like a mistake. (And that's without even accounting for the fact that they might get both Roman Anthony and Garrett Crochet back before the regular season ends.)

No. 6 San Diego Padres over No. 3 Atlanta Braves No. 5 Philadelphia Phillies over No. 4 Chicago Cubs

No. 1 Los Angeles Dodgers over No. 5 Philadelphia Phillies No. 2 Milwaukee Brewers over No. 6 San Diego Padres

NLCS : No. 1 Los Angeles Dodgers over No. 2 Milwaukee Brewers

The biggest X-factor on the NL half of the bracket is how much the Phillies will get outside of their big six of Cristopher Sánchez, Zack Wheeler, Jesús Luzardo, Jhoan Duran, Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper.

In winning 16 of their first 21 games of August, they've gotten a ton of production from Bryson Stott, Alec Bohm, Justin Crawford and trade deadline acquisition Luis Arraez, not to mention four straight solid outings from Aaron Nola. If that continues, they could be the perfect foil to the Dodgers and a fantastic candidate to win the World Series.

The Brewers are also a more legitimate threat to the LA dynasty than they were last year, as evidenced by their taking three out of four from the Dodgers a week ago. Granted, they went 6-0 against Los Angeles during the 2025 regular season before getting swept in the NLCS, but their starting rotation has blossomed from "above average" last year to "maybe the best in baseball" this year.

The only thing we're reasonably confident in is that the Cubs don't have the pitching to navigate this gauntlet. But who knows? They could just mash their way through October like the Rangers did in 2023.

Los Angeles Dodgers over Boston Red Sox (in 6 games)

Love them or hate them, the Dodgers are following their tried and true World Series blueprint to a tee:

Assert dominance through the first three months

Sputter for a month or so starting around July 4

Turn things back around in mid-August and enter the postseason on a tear

They're only partway through that third step, but they sure seemed to have snapped out of that 11-17 funk that temporarily dropped them behind Atlanta in the race for the first-round byes.

Blake Snell is back and already reminding everyone of his career splits as a drastically better pitcher in the second half. Tyler Glasnow returns on Tuesday. Tarik Skubal got his first win with the Dodgers on Saturday, a few hours after Shohei Ohtani threw a 30-pitch live batting practice in his quest to resume his unicorn ways. And, of course, Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been their rock all season long.

The thermal exhaust port on this Death Star could be the closer situation if they try to force Edwin Díaz back into that role again when he comes off the IL. Also, the outfield has gotten pretty bleak now that Andy Pages is out indefinitely with a fractured hand.

But the expectation all season long has been that a Dodgers three-peat would be the final straw before a contentious lockout, and that still appears to be the case.

articles.title: Latest New York Yankees Playoff Predictions, Updated Player Stats, Injuries, Standings
articles.summary: With five weeks remaining in the 2026 Major League Baseball season, the New York Yankees have been playing some of their best baseball as of late, threatening to reclaim first place in the AL East for what would be a critical first-round bye in the postseason.
articles.body:
With five weeks remaining in the 2026 Major League Baseball season, the New York Yankees have been playing some of their best baseball as of late, threatening to reclaim first place in the AL East for what would be a critical first-round bye in the postseason.

Ahead, we'll take a look at which Yankees have been hot over the past week, what's on tap for the upcoming week, some injury updates and the current standings before offering up fresh predictions for October.

You can't ask for much better than five wins in six games against division rivals.

It would've been sweeter if it had come against the Rays and Red Sox, but the Yankees swept the Orioles in Baltimore before taking two out of three at home against the Blue Jays. Dylan Cease flirting yet again with a no-hitter was the only thing that could slow the Yankees down.

During that surge, Spencer Jones had maybe his best week yet in the majors, going 8-for-21 (.381 AVG) with two home runs, two stolen bases and seven runs scored.

The real star, though, was the pitching staff. Cam Schlittler and Gerrit Cole each went six innings of one-run ball—the former lowering his ERA to a still AL-best 2.16—while the bullpen had a cumulative ERA of 1.35. The Yankees have now held their opponent to five runs or fewer in 17 consecutive games, winning 11 of them.

The homestand continues with two series featuring major postseason implications.

First up, the Yankees host the Houston Astros on Tuesday-Thursday, with the sub-500 visitors desperately trying to hang onto first place in the AL West.

Since signing with the Yankees in 2020, Cole has made just three starts against his former employer. But he has destroyed the Astros each time, allowing three runs in 23 innings of work. He has also been hot as of late with a 2.45 ERA since the beginning of July. Look for him to turn in another gem on Wednesday as the Yankees do their best to stifle Yordan Alvarez's bat.

But the much, much bigger series is the four games in three days against the Red Sox.

It's such a key series, in fact, that the Yankees might want to think about giving Schlittler (who should start on Thursday against Houston) an extra day of rest to start on Friday, hoping he can go deep in the series opener to help preserve the bullpen for the combination of Saturday's doubleheader and the early game on Sunday.

An additional motivating factor in that decision could be that Schlittler has owned the Red Sox in his young career. In three starts against them this season, he has a 0.96 ERA—this after his all-time postseason gem (8.0 IP, 5 H, 0 R, 12 K) in the do-or-die Game 3 of the 2025 Wild Card series.

Where the Yankees turn from there, though, remains to be seen. Saturday could be an intriguing "all hands on deck" showdown with their loathed rival.

Both Carlos Rodón (elbow) and Cody Bellinger (hamstring) returned from the IL this week. The former lasted four innings in each of his starts on Tuesday and Sunday, but was reasonably effective for those four innings, allowing one earned run in each. The latter came back on Sunday after nearly a full month on the shelf and went 1-for-4.

Max Fried (elbow) threw a 26-pitch bullpen on Saturday and Aaron Judge (rib) progressed to hitting off a tee this week. There's a reasonable chance both will return in early-to-mid September. Clarke Schmidt (Tommy John) also might be able to make it back as a reliever, slated to begin a rehab assignment within the next week.

Ryan McMahon (thumb) landed on the IL on Thursday, but with just one home run and a .630 OPS thus far in the second half, that's not a catastrophic loss. More José Caballero probably isn't a bad thing.

Ryan Weathers (forearm) was lost to the IL after an early exit from his start on Saturday. And with a stretch of 10 games in nine days beginning on Tuesday, that's a real bummer. They were already probably going to need to call up either Elmer Rodríguez or Luis Gil (who is recovering from a shoulder injury) from Triple-A for a spot start to survive this crunch, but now they might need to lean on both for a pivotal stretch of the schedule.

Worse yet, Giancarlo Stanton suffered a setback in his quest to return from the IL, injuring his left calf while running the bases in his rehab from a right calf strain. Whether he'll be able to return in 2026 is now questionable at best .

Barring what would be maybe the most catastrophic late-season collapse in MLB history, the Yankees are going to make the postseason. At any rate, PECOTA , FanGraphs and Baseball-Reference each put New York's playoff odds at 99.9 percent, and good luck finding a sportsbook that even offers a line on the Yankees making/missing the postseason at this point, 18 games above .500 in a league that only has four teams with a winning record.

Whether they'll land the No. 1, No. 4 or No. 5 seed, though, is the great unknown.

New York is three games behind Tampa Bay for first place in the AL East, as well as three games ahead of Boston for the top wild card spot. It has four games remaining against each of those division rivals, but also has the easiest remaining schedule of the trio, including three home games against the Rockies, three home games against the Mets and a three-game set on the road against the Angels.

The opportunity is absolutely there for the Yankees to take over the top spot, though the likeliest scenario at this point remains securing the No. 4 seed and hosting the Red Sox in the wild card round for a second consecutive year.

That could be bad news, though, as Boston has been a blistering inferno for a while now, boasting a .750 winning percentage over its last 52 games—a two-month stretch that began with a four-game sweep of the Yankees at Fenway Park.

If that series began today—with no Aaron Judge, no Max Fried and Boston seemingly unable to be stopped—we'd have to forecast the Red Sox to win, regardless of New York's home-field advantage.

However, that feeling could change in a big way after this weekend's showdown with Boston. And if the Yankees survive that initial best-of-three series, there's a good chance they'd take down Tampa Bay in the ALDS before also beating whoever is left standing in the ALCS to reach the World Series.

articles.title: MLB Power Rankings as Phillies Catch Fire, Braves Cool Off and Tigers Season Slips Away
articles.summary: With five full weeks of the regular season remaining, a staggering 20 of the league's 30 teams are still within five games of a playoff spot.
articles.body:
With five full weeks of the regular season remaining, a staggering 20 of the league's 30 teams are still within five games of a playoff spot.

That includes 12 of the 15 American League teams, as the AL Central title, AL West title and final wild-card berth are all truly wide open entering the stretch run of the season.

Even the teams that have fallen out of the race are still capable of making noise, as the Kansas City Royals have shown with eight straight wins out of the AL Central cellar.

While everyone is still chasing the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers, it does feel like the parity across Major League Baseball is at an all-time high behind that budding dynasty.

In case you missed it, B/R's MLB Power Rankings from last week and every fresh power rankings throughout the season can be found at the new MLB Power Rankings hub .

30. Colorado Rockies (50-80) 29. San Francisco Giants (52-78) 28. Los Angeles Angels (52-79) 27. Athletics (51-80) 26. Washington Nationals (61-71) 25. Cincinnati Reds (62-69) 24. Kansas City Royals (58-74) 23. New York Mets (59-72)

-The longest winning streak in baseball right now belongs to the Phillies at nine in a row, but the Royals are right behind them as winners of eight straight after sweeping the Athletics and Tigers. Their reward? The club's playoff odds at FanGraphs have climbed from 0.0 to 0.1 percent.

-The Angels and Athletics both took two of three from the Astros in Houston, and with that there are now zero teams in the AL West with a winning record. Shortstop Zach Neto went 14-for-28 with seven extra-base hits in six games for the Angels last week.

-The Mets have baseball's fifth-toughest remaining schedule with one series each against the Brewers, Marlins, Phillies, Rays and Yankees. After picking up a series win over the Padres last week, they could continue to play spoiler throughout September.

22. Detroit Tigers (61-69) 21. Pittsburgh Pirates (63-69) 20. Minnesota Twins (63-68) 19. St. Louis Cardinals (66-66)

-With a 1-5 week, the Tigers tumbled from second to fourth in the AL Central standings, and their longshot playoff hopes were dealt a major blow. Zooming out, they are 2-9 in their last 11 games and could fall to the bottom group as early as next week.

-The Twins (7-13) and Pirates (8-13) have been two of the worst teams in baseball in August, and what were legitimate wild-card aspirations at the beginning of the month have faded into the background.

-The Cardinals have been the definition of middling this season, with a .500 record, a negative-two run differential, a 32-34 record at home and a 34-32 record on the road. They also rank 16th in runs scored and 17th in team ERA.

18. Seattle Mariners (62-69) 17. Toronto Blue Jays (64-68) 16. Baltimore Orioles (63-68) 15. Houston Astros (65-66)

-The Mariners have the easiest remaining schedule of any team in baseball based on the combined winning percentage of the opposition, while the Blue Jays are a close second and do not play another game against a team that currently has a winning record.

-Slugger Pete Alonso is hitting .321/.399/.573 with nine home runs and 20 RBI in 34 games since the All-Star break. He officially logged his sixth straight 30-homer season with a long ball on Friday, and he has done exactly what was expected when he inked a five-year, $155 million deal with the Orioles during the offseason.

-A 16-6 stretch of games helped the Astros build a season-high three-game lead in the AL West standings entering play on Aug. 15, but three straight series losses at home to the Mariners, Angels and Athletics have brought that momentum to a screeching halt.

14. Miami Marlins (67-64) 13. Cleveland Guardians (65-66) 12. Texas Rangers (65-66) 11. Chicago White Sox (68-62)

-The Marlins continue to hang around in the wild-card picture thanks to a stellar 41-25 record at home this season, and they padded those numbers with a three-game sweep of the Nationals last week. The flip side of that is a 26-39 mark on the road, and those struggles were perfectly illustrated when they were swept by the Phillies prior to that Nationals series.

-The Guardians (2-1 vs. SF, 3-0 @ COL) and Rangers (2-1 vs. WAS, 2-1 vs. LAA) were the biggest risers in this week's rankings, with both jumping up from the "Facing an Uphill Battle" tier. The two clubs are currently tied for the third AL wild-card spot, while the Rangers also share the AL West lead with the Astros.

-The White Sox entered last week with a season-high 5.5-game lead in the AL Central race, but a 3-4 week that included a series loss to the crosstown rival Cubs has narrowed that advantage to 3.5 games. Rising star Miguel Vargas had eight hits and 10 walks in seven games.

Arizona has remained in the wild-card hunt amid an off-field development involving Ketel Marte. Beyond Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado, the D-backs may not have much name recognition among casual fans, but they are very much alive in the playoff race.

The Padres suffered their first series loss since July 23 when they dropped two of three to the Mets last week, but they quickly rallied to sweep the Twins over the weekend. A red-hot Fernando Tatis Jr. went 12-for-25 with four home runs and 11 RBI last week, and he is now up to 17 long balls after not hitting his first of the year until May 30.

Previous Rank: No. 5 Last Week: 0-3 @ MIN, 1-0 @ CWS, 1-2 @ MIL

The Braves have lost four of their last five series, going 6-11 during that stretch, and what was once a commanding 8.5-game lead in the NL East is now a mere three-game edge over the streaking Phillies. Things don't get any easier this week as they welcome the Dodgers to town on Tuesday.

Previous Rank: No. 10 Last Week: 2-1 vs. ARI, 3-0 vs. SF

After the Rays and Yankees, the Red Sox have the best odds to make the postseason of any AL team by a wide margin, despite currently sitting in the No. 2 wild-card spot. Deadline pickup Erik Miller has not allowed an earned run in 8.1 innings since joining the Red Sox, logging a 14-to-3 strikeout-to-walk ratio while emerging as the primary bridge to Aroldis Chapman.

Previous Rank: No. 4 Last Week: 1-0 vs. BAL, 1-2 vs. TOR, 1-2 @ BAL

Despite some bumps along the way, the Rays have been atop the AL East standings since June 28, though a pair of series losses last week has the Yankees nipping at their heels just three games back. With five more home runs, Junior Caminero will become the first player in franchise history with multiple 40-homer campaigns.

Previous Rank: No. 8 Last Week: 3-0 vs. MIA, 3-0 vs. STL

The Phillies have outscored the opposition by 34 runs during their current nine-game winning streak, and they rank second in the majors with 122 runs scored over 21 games in August. A nine-game, West Coast road trip against the Mariners, Angels and Diamondbacks will put their momentum to the test, though they are a terrific 35-28 away from Citizens Bank Park this year.

Previous Rank: No. 2 Last Week: 2-1 vs. CWS, 1-2 @ SEA

Another week, another impressive stat line from Pete Crow-Armstrong. The NL MVP candidate went 9-for-24 with five home runs, including a leadoff and walk-off blast in the same game on Monday when he also secured a second straight 30/30 season. The North Siders are now the highest-scoring team in baseball with 684 runs in 131 games.

Previous Rank: No. 6 Last Week: 3-0 @ BAL, 2-1 vs. TOR

The Yankees welcomed back Cody Bellinger on Sunday after he missed 25 games with a hamstring injury, and an MLB-best 2.75 ERA in August has helped prop up an offense that was without him and Aaron Judge. The rival Red Sox await for a huge three-game series at Yankee Stadium this weekend.

Previous Rank: No. 3 Last Week: 3-0 @ COL, 3-0 vs. PIT

Blake Snell threw a gem on Sunday (6.0 IP, 2 H, 0 ER), Tyler Glasnow is set to be activated from the injured list on Tuesday for his first start since May 6 and the Dodgers have won six in a row. They have seemingly weathered the storm of a seven-game losing streak earlier this month and come out the other side geared up for another deep October run.

Previous Rank: No. 1 Last Week: 2-1 vs. SEA, 2-1 vs. ATL

There was no letdown from the Brewers following their series win over the Dodgers, as they plated a season-high 22 runs against the Mariners last Tuesday and ultimately walked away with two more series wins. With six shutout innings on Friday, NL Cy Young front-runner Jacob Misiorowski now has a 1.68 ERA, 0.76 WHIP and 216 strikeouts in 145 innings, and he has allowed just 77 hits for a .152 opponents' batting average.

articles.title: Astros, GM Dana Brown 'Part Ways' Despite Being No. 1 Seed in AL West Standings
articles.summary: The Houston Astros announced Monday they reached a mutual agreement to relieve general manager Dana Brown of his duties.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros announced Monday they reached a mutual agreement to relieve general manager Dana Brown of his duties.

"Over the past four seasons, Dana has helped our organization win two division titles and has led our baseball front office through key scouting, draft and development efforts," owner Jim Crane said. "On behalf of the Astros, I want to thank him for his commitment, energy, and contributions to our organization. We wish he and his family the best."

Meanwhile, Joe Espada's status as manager has not changed, according to Chandler Rome of The Athletic. Per Rome, Espada "has not been told anything about his future beyond this season." He reportedly has not had any conversations about his future.

Brown's exit comes as the Astros are tied for first place in the American League West, though they're a game under .500 (65-66).

Brown's departure has been a long time coming.

Back in June 2024, The Athletic's Chandler Rome wrote how there were questions over how much authority the GM had behind the scenes. Special advisors Reggie Jackson, Jeff Bagwell and Craig Biggio were providing their own input on personnel moves.

Going back two more years, before Brown was hired, Bagwell weighed in to say the organization had leaned too much on analytics despite that approach helping to deliver a pair of World Series titles.

The Hall of Fame first baseman is now part of the group that will share Brown's usual everyday duties.

The Astros' record has steadily gotten worse since their last World Series win in 2022. They registered 90, 88 and 87 wins over the next three years, and now they're on track for their worst finish in a full 162-game season since 2014. Winning the AL West wouldn't hide the fact the roster isn't good enough right now.

Brown undoubtedly has a role in that, but he's not solely to blame for the state of the franchise.

A downturn was inevitable as the key players from their 2017 championship team got older and too expensive to retain over time. The organizational shift in team-building strategy hasn't been a net-positive, either.

Bagwell played a role in the disastrous signing of José Abreu during the 2023 offseason. Crane helped influence the return of Carlos Correa at the 2025 trade deadline, and Correa's sizable contract is aging worse and worse.

In general, the results from Houston's win-now moves speak for themselves. They have a top-10 payroll and one of MLB's worst farm systems . That's a rough combination for a team that looks so far away from seriously contending.

The obvious concern as it relates to the Astros' GM search is whether Crane is willing to let Brown's replacement execute a long-term plan as they see fit.

articles.title: Rob Manfred Says MLB, MLBPA Meet 'Regularly' for CBA Talks Amid Salary Cap Buzz
articles.summary: MLB commissioner Rob Manfred told ESPN on Sunday that "we're planning on playing baseball next year" amidst mounting pessimism about the ongoing collective bargaining negotiations and the possibility of a lockout in 2027.
articles.body:
MLB commissioner Rob Manfred told ESPN on Sunday that "we're planning on playing baseball next year" amidst mounting pessimism about the ongoing collective bargaining negotiations and the possibility of a lockout in 2027.

"We're meeting regularly, which is good," he added during the Little League Classic regarding those labor talks. "Every week, we've had days where we've met with the players. It's early, but we've got a lot of work to do, and we're at it. Look, our goal is to make a deal. We want to make a deal. We want to play baseball next year. We're planning on playing baseball next year."

The main hurdle in negotiations is the desire from the owners to add a salary cap, something the MLBPA has consistently said it would never accept. The players, meanwhile, are seeking a higher minimum salary, reduced restrictions on the luxury tax threshold and improvements to the bonus pool before arbitration.

Most fans want more competitive balance, annoyed that teams like the Dodgers seem to endlessly add talent and salary while five MLB franchises currently have a payroll less than $100 million. There's a strong argument to be made that more competitive balance could be added by increasing the payroll floor, adding stricter rules regarding deferred contracts and finding unique ways to increase revenue sharing, however.

Players have argued that a salary cap would limit their earning potential in the long term and that the owners are largely seeking a cap to increase franchise valuations . It also would be complicated for teams set to have payrolls above the $245.3 million hard cap in future seasons, or for teams dramatically below the owners' proposed $171.2 million floor. Some sort of grace period, perhaps over multiple seasons, would be necessary.

Either way, the expectation remains that the owners will lock out the players if a salary cap isn't accepted. Regardless of Manfred's remarks, the 2027 season remains very much in jeopardy.

articles.title: Jacob Young Reacts to 'Spider-Man' Wall Catch After Epic HR Robbery Highlight for Nationals
articles.summary: Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.
articles.body:
Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.

Young has been given the Spider-Man nickname in the past, and it sure seemed apt after that grab.

"It's a fun one," he told MLB.com's Perla Paredes regarding the nickname. "But you know, if [I] keep catching the ball, [the fans] can call me whatever they want."

As for scaling the wall to make the grab, Young called it "instinctual" and said that his mindset is to just "go try to catch everything."

"It just kind of ended up in the spot where I like to climb them," he added. "And I'm gonna give myself a chance. And when I looked up, the ball was there, so it was cool to be able to get [Jackson] a couple more innings and keep us in the game."

The Nationals ultimately lost 6-2 anyway, but at least Young provided one of the season's best highlights.
